subject: Maths
title: Adding and subtracting decimals
subtitle: Decimals — All Operations · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can add and subtract decimals using column methods, lining up the decimal points.

key_vocab.definition: When adding or subtracting decimals, line up the decimal points so that digits with the same place value are in the same column.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can add and subtract decimals using column methods, lining up the decimal points.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: decimals -- When adding or subtracting decimals, line up the decimal points so that digits with the same place value are in the same column.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Line up the decimal points. Fill empty places with zeros. Then add or subtract as normal.
12.45 + 3.60 = 16.05
Pad with zeros to match decimal places

Key examples:
  ✓ 3.5 + 2.7 = 6.2  (line up points)
  ✓ 5.0 − 1.3 = 3.7  (use placeholder 0)
  ✓ 12.45 + 3.6 = 16.05  (3.6 = 3.60)
  ✗ 3.5 + 2.7 = 5.12  (not place value error)
  ✗ 1.3 + 2.45 lined up without point  (must align decimals)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – adding
  Calculate 4.3 + 2.8
  Line up: 4.3 + 2.8
  3 + 8 = 11, write 1 carry 1
  4 + 2 + 1 = 7 → 7.1
  = 7.1
  (Carry works exactly the same as with whole numbers.)

Example 2 – different decimal places
  Calculate 5.6 + 3.45
  Write as 5.60 + 3.45
  0 + 5 = 5; 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 carry 1
  5 + 3 + 1 = 9 → 9.05
  = 9.05
  (Pad 5.6 with a zero to make 5.60.)

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
Show your column working.

(a) Buy items at £3.49 and £2.75. Total?
(b) Had £20; spent £13.62. Change?
(c) Run 3.5 km then 2.75 km. Total?
(d) Rope 8 m; cut off 2.35 m. Left?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Line up decimal points when adding
✗ 3.5 + 2.7 = 5.12
✓ 10 − 3.46 = 6.54
✓ 4.5 is the same as 4.50
✗ 1.3 + 2.45 = 3.48
